page: Microsoft Azure D128ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz across an x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources comprise 128 dedicated vCPUs spanning 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache. Memory provision equals 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage features 7559 GB of integrated NVMe SSD space. The server does not include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory access speeds. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (116506.62) and Geekbench multi-core execution (21171.0). Large block read memory bandwidth reaches 511.08 GB/sec uncached, paired with 8837.3 GB/sec in cached small block tests. Hardware-assisted instructions, including AVX-512 and AMX matrix acceleration, yield high-tier scores across PassMark CPU extended tests and clang software compilation benchmarks. Single-core performance falls in the moderate to strong range, showing 1949.68 in stress-ng and 2134.0 in Geekbench single-core evaluations.

Storage and cache-dependent workloads benefit from the integrated 7559 GB NVMe SSD and high multi-threaded decompression rates (742.86 GB/sec in bzip3). PassMark database operations and Redis SET testing registered top-decile throughput, logging 156.93 million Redis operations per second. Static web serving throughput also places in the top tier at 171.91 GB/sec. LLM inference shows balanced capabilities on smaller models, delivering 3355.11 prompt processing tokens per second on a 135M parameter model, though throughput is limited for heavier generation tasks due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

The D128ds_v6 provides high computational density and extensive NVMe capacity within a balanced resource framework. It is structurally aligned with large-scale relational and NoSQL databases, enterprise in-memory caches, distributed compilation pipelines, static web traffic handling, and heavy multi-threaded enterprise application hosting.

It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, but excludes dedicated GPUs. Single-thread processing registers within the expected enterprise average. The resource profile is engineered for high-concurrency enterprise workloads, distributed databases, large-scale build farms, and memory-intensive caching tiers.
